coreIdea: Connected needs ≥n-1 edges (tree). Max simple graph edges = C(n,2). Cut vertex/bridge = never part of a cycle. Cayley: K_n has n^(n-2) spanning trees.
mustRememberFormulas: Min edges connected = n-1; Max simple = n(n-1)/2
Max edges with k components = (n-k)(n-k+1)/2 (concentrate into one component)
Cayley's formula: spanning trees of K_n = n^(n-2)
(A^k)[i][j] = walks of length k, i to j. Triangles = trace(A³)/6
Eulerian circuit iff connected + all degrees even

commonTrapsQuickList: 'Max edges with k components' concentrates edges into ONE component, not evenly split
Cut vertex/bridge is NEVER part of a cycle — check cycle membership to disprove
Cayley's formula (n^(n-2)) only applies to COMPLETE graphs, not general graphs
Hamiltonian cycles have NO simple degree-based existence test, unlike Eulerian circuits
highYieldPyqLessons: Edge-counting formulas (13/40) are the single highest-ROI sub-skill — a fixed formula library with direct lookup, memorize once.
This topic is the Discrete-Math mirror of Graph Search + MST — the same structural intuitions (components, cuts, trees) appear from a proof/counting angle here instead of an algorithmic one.
